source.title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction

accepted.question_text: Let L be a positive continuous function on C^n. For a nonzero direction c in C^n, say that an entire function H has bounded L-index in direction c if there is an integer m0 such that, for every point z and every m >= 0, |D_c^m H(z)|/(m! L(z)^m) is at most the maximum of |D_c^k H(z)|/(k! L(z)^k) over 0 <= k <= m0, where D_c is the directional derivative in direction c. Suppose f1 and f2 are entire functions of bounded L-index in the corresponding directions b1 and b2, and h is entire. For the first-order partial differential equation f1(z) D_b1 F(z) + f2(z) D_b2 F(z) = h(z), what direction b and what additional conditions on the data ensure that an entire solution F has bounded L-index in direction b?

Let L be a positive continuous function and use the bounded directional L-index definition: H has bounded L-index in direction c if the normalized directional derivatives |D_c^m H(z)|/(m! L(z)^m) are controlled, for all m and z, by finitely many orders 0 <= k <= m0. If g(z1,z2) is an entire function of bounded L-index in both directions b1 and b2, what positive function L* and direction b* ensure that an entire solution F of the mixed directional equation D_b1 D_b2 F(z1,z2) = g(z1,z2) has bounded L*-index in direction b*?

Let L be positive and continuous on C^2, and call an entire function H of bounded L-index in direction c when finitely many normalized directional derivatives |D_c^k H(z)|/(k! L(z)^k), 0 <= k <= m0, dominate every normalized order m at every point. Suppose P1(z1,z2) and P2(z1,z2) are entire functions of bounded L-index in the coordinate directions (1,0) and (0,1), respectively. For the equation P1(z1,z2) partial F/partial z1 + P2(z1,z2) partial F/partial z2 = h(z1,z2), what direction b and what additional assumptions imply that an entire solution F has bounded L-index in direction b?

For an entire function of two variables f(z,w), assume f has bounded L-index in the two coordinate directions (1,0) and (0,1), meaning that in each direction its normalized directional derivatives are controlled by finitely many lower orders using the positive function L. For the ordinary differential equation w'(z) = f(z,w(z)), what one-variable positive function l should be chosen, and under what conditions, so that an entire solution w has bounded l-index in the ordinary one-variable sense?

Let l be a positive continuous function of one complex variable, and say that an entire function has bounded l-index if finitely many normalized derivatives |f^(k)(z)|/(k! l(z)^k) dominate all normalized derivative orders at every z. If f(z) has bounded l-index and w is an entire solution of the infinite-order linear differential equation sum_{k=0}^infty a_k w^(k)(z) = f(z), what assumptions on the coefficients a_k and on f(z) guarantee that w also has bounded l-index?

Let L be a positive continuous function in the class Q_b^n, meaning that along every complex line z + tb in direction b the ratios L(z+tb)/L(z+t0 b) are bounded above and below away from 0 on scaled discs |t-t0| <= eta/L(z+t0 b), uniformly in z and t0 for each eta. For an entire function F on C^n, is bounded L-index in direction b equivalent to the following single-scale maximum-minimum condition: there exist R > 0, P2(R) >= 1, and eta(R) in (0,R) such that for every z0 in C^n and t0 in C, some r in [eta(R),R] satisfies max{|F(z0+tb)| : |t-t0| = r/L(z0+t0 b)} <= P2(R) min{|F(z0+tb)| : |t-t0| = r/L(z0+t0 b)}?

Let F be entire on C^n and L be in Q_b^n. For each b-line t -> F(z0+tb), let G_r^b(F) be the union of scaled r-neighborhoods, measured with L, around the zeros of these one-variable slices. Is F of bounded L-index in direction b if and only if there is a single r > 0 and constants P > 0 and n_tilde such that (1) outside G_r^b(F), the logarithmic directional derivative satisfies |D_b F(z)/F(z)| <= P L(z), and (2) on every nonzero slice t -> F(z0+tb), each scaled disc of radius r/(|b| L(z0+t0 b)) contains at most n_tilde zeros?
accepted.context_brief: Logarithmic derivative and zero counting criterion

accepted.question_text: Can one construct an entire function F on C^n, a positive continuous function L, two disjoint unbounded domains G1 and G2 whose union is C^n, and two directions b1 and b2 such that F satisfies the bounded L-index defining inequality in direction b1 throughout G1 and in direction b2 throughout G2, but fails that same bounded-index inequality in direction b2 on G1 and in direction b1 on G2?

Can one choose complex numbers a1, a2, c1, and c2, together with an entire function F(z1,z2), so that F(z1,z2) has bounded L-index in a fixed direction b = (b1,b2), but the affine coordinate change G(z1,z2) = F(a1 z1 + c1, a2 z2 + c2) has unbounded L-index in that same direction b = (b1,b2)?

For entire functions on C^n and a positive continuous function L, what is the smallest or least set A of directions with the following property: whenever an entire function F has bounded L-index in every direction b in A, it follows that F has bounded L-index in every nonzero direction b in C^n?

Let {b1,...,bn} be a basis of C^n. Suppose F is entire on C^n and has bounded L-index in each basis direction bi, with L belonging to the corresponding class Q_bi^n for each i. Must F then have bounded L-index in every nonzero direction b that is a complex linear combination b = lambda1 b1 + ... + lambdan bn?

Fix a direction b and an entire function F on C^n with positive continuous L. For each base point z0, define the one-variable slice g_z0(t) = F(z0 + tb) and the slice weight l_z0(t) = L(z0 + tb). What minimal requirements on a set A of base points are enough to ensure that the global directional index N_b(F,L) equals max{N(g_z0,l_z0) : z0 in A}, where N(g_z0,l_z0) is the one-variable l_z0-index of the slice?

Consider an entire product in C^n with planar zeros, pi(z) = product_{k>=1} g(<z,a_k>|a_k|^{-2},p), where g(u,p) = (1-u) exp(u + u^2/2 + ... + u^p/p) for p != 0 and g(u,0) = 1-u, and where the sequence a_k has genus p through sum |a_k|^{-p-1} < infinity and sum |a_k|^{-p} = infinity. Existing sufficient conditions for bounded L-index in a direction assume the zero-defining vectors lie on a fixed ray, a_kj = m_j |a_k|. Are there sufficient conditions for bounded L-index in a direction for such products without imposing that fixed-ray condition?

Given two nonparallel directions b1 and b2, construct an entire function with planar zeros, in the sense of zeros coming from factors g(<z,a_k>|a_k|^{-2},p), that has bounded L-index in direction b1 but unbounded L-index in direction b2.

Let F:C^{n+m}->C be entire, let L1:C^n->R+ and L2:C^m->R+ be positive functions, and split variables into a first block of n coordinates and a second block of m coordinates. Suppose that, for every fixed second block, F has uniformly bounded L1-index in the direction (b1,...,bn,0,...,0), and for every fixed first block, F has uniformly bounded L2-index in the direction (0,...,0,b_{n+1},...,b_{n+m}). What positive function L:C^{n+m}->R+ makes F have bounded L-index in the combined direction b = (b1,...,b_{n+m})?
accepted.context_brief: Combining bounded indices across variable blocks

accepted.question_text: Let l:C->R+ be continuous, let e_j be the j-th coordinate direction in C^n, and write l_j(z) = l(z_j). Suppose that for each j = 1,...,n-1 an entire function F has bounded l_j-index in direction e_j, and that for every fixed (z1,...,z_{n-1}) the function of the remaining variable z_n has bounded l_n-index. Prove, or determine whether it is true, that F has bounded l_n-index in direction e_n.

What conditions on the zero set and growth of an entire function F(z1,z2) provide both of the following properties: for every base point (z1^0,z2^0) in C^2, the one-variable slice t -> F(z1^0 + b1 t, z2^0 + b2 t) has bounded index, but the two-variable function F(z1,z2) has unbounded L-index in the direction b = (b1,b2)?
accepted.context_brief: Bounded slice indices with unbounded directional index

accepted.question_text: For n >= 3, construct an entire function F of n complex variables, a nonzero direction b = (b1,...,bn), and a positive continuous function L such that every one-variable slice t -> F(z0 + tb) has bounded l_z0-index for l_z0(t) = L(z0 + tb), while the full function F(z) has unbounded L-index in direction b.
